content: The evidence review combined data from multiple cohorts with varying follow-up durations after the initiation of treatment. For example, the WHO IPD 2021 dataset included cohorts with different follow-up times. Follow-up time was divided into two periods: the time from treatment initiation to treatment completion and the time from treatment completion to the end of follow-up. For shorter treatment regimens, post-treatment follow-up was particularly critical due to the potential for higher relapse rates, which may result from incomplete eradication of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It was essential to ensure equivalent follow-up durations between comparison groups to provide participants with equal chances of experiencing outcomes such as death or relapse. In these analyses, follow-up time was measured from the start of treatment rather than from treatment completion to minimize the impact of differences in total follow-up time. Follow-up was limited to 24 months after treatment initiation across all cohorts. No analyses included both intervention and comparator cohorts with follow-up durations exceeding 24 months. Evidence from tuberculosis (TB) treatment trials indicates that a significant proportion of recurrences occur within 6 to 12 months after stopping treatment. Primary analyses were designed to maximize the number of participants included in both groups. For shorter regimens (6–9 months), follow-up was extended to capture potential relapses. Additional sensitivity analyses were conducted, where feasible, to evaluate the impact of follow-up time on treatment outcomes. The evidence on novel regimens to address PICO questions was derived from two trials: TB-PRACTECAL and ZeNix. These trials included data from 419 of 423 participants in four arms of TB-PRACTECAL and 172 of 181 participants in four arms of ZeNix. Data from relevant trial arms were used in comparisons that informed conclusions and final recommendations on the use of the BPaLM/BPaL regimen. Some participants were excluded due to unconfirmed rifampicin resistance. For example, the BPaL 1200–9 arm of the ZeNix trial (linezolid 1200 mg daily for 9 weeks) was compared with the BPaL 1200–26 arm (linezolid 1200 mg daily for 26 weeks) in patients with multidrug-resistant or rifampicin-resistant TB (MDR/RR-TB), with or without fluoroquinolone resistance. The primary analysis was conducted at 12 months post-treatment initiation. The Guideline Development Group (GDG) judged the benefits of BPaL with linezolid 1200–9 to be small and the undesirable effects moderate compared to BPaL with linezolid 1200–26. The certainty of evidence was very low. Based on this, the panel concluded that the balance of health effects likely favors BPaL with linezolid 1200–26. Consequently, the use of 26 weeks of 1200 mg linezolid is suggested over 9 weeks of 1200 mg linezolid as part of the BPaL regimen in adults with MDR/RR-TB or pre-extensively drug-resistant TB (pre-XDR-TB). The BPaL 600–26 arm of the ZeNix trial (linezolid 600 mg daily for 26 weeks) was compared with the BPaL 1200–26 arm (linezolid 1200 mg daily for 26 weeks) in the same population. The primary analysis was conducted at 12 months post-treatment initiation. The GDG judged the benefits of BPaL with linezolid 600–26 to be moderate and the undesirable effects trivial compared to BPaL with linezolid 1200–26. The certainty of evidence was very low. Based on this, the panel concluded that the balance of health effects likely favors BPaL with linezolid 600–26. Therefore, the use of 26 weeks of 600 mg linezolid over 26 weeks of 1200 mg linezolid is suggested as part of the BPaL regimen in adults with MDR/RR-TB or pre-XDR-TB. The BPaL 600–9 arm of the ZeNix trial (linezolid 600 mg daily for 9 weeks) was compared with the BPaL 1200–26 arm (linezolid 1200 mg daily for 26 weeks) in the same population. The primary analysis was conducted at 12 months post-treatment initiation. The GDG judged the benefits of BPaL with linezolid 600–9 to be small and the undesirable effects moderate compared to BPaL with linezolid 1200–26. The certainty of evidence was very low. Based on this, the panel concluded that the balance of health effects likely favors BPaL with linezolid 1200–26. Consequently, the use of 26 weeks of 1200 mg linezolid over 9 weeks of 600 mg linezolid is suggested as part of the BPaL regimen in adults with MDR/RR-TB or pre-XDR-TB. The assessment of PICO 3 allowed for the determination of the optimal dosing and duration of linezolid within the BPaLM/BPaL regimen. This narrowed subsequent comparisons to the intervention regimen with a specific dose and duration of linezolid—BPaL (600 mg for 26 weeks). The BPaL 600–26 arm of the ZeNix trial (linezolid 600 mg daily for 26 weeks) was compared with a cohort of MDR/RR-TB patients with fluoroquinolone resistance from the 2021 IPD, who were treated with longer regimens designed in accordance with 2020 WHO guidelines. The primary analysis was conducted at 18 months post-treatment initiation. The GDG judged the benefits of BPaL with linezolid 600–26 to be large and the undesirable effects moderate compared to longer regimens recommended by WHO. The certainty of evidence was very low. Based on this, the panel concluded that the balance of health effects likely favors BPaL with linezolid 600–26. Therefore, the use of the 6-month treatment regimen composed of bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid (BPaL) rather than a longer (18-month) regimen is suggested in patients with MDR/RR-TB and resistance to fluoroquinolones (pre-XDR-TB), who have either had no previous exposure to bedaquiline and linezolid or have been exposed for less than 1 month. The assessment of PICO 4 resulted in a conditional recommendation for the use of the BPaL (600 mg for 26 weeks) regimen over the currently recommended longer regimens in patients with MDR/RR-TB and additional fluoroquinolone resistance (pre-XDR-TB). The BPaL 600–26 arm of the ZeNix trial (linezolid 600 mg daily for 26 weeks) was compared with a cohort of MDR/RR-TB patients without fluoroquinolone resistance treated in South Africa with the WHO-recommended 9-month regimen with ethionamide for 4 months. The primary analysis was conducted at 12 months post-treatment initiation. Grade 3–5 adverse events were noted in 14% of participants receiving the BPaL 600–26 regimen, but no comparison could be made due to the lack of data for participants receiving the 9-month regimen with ethionamide. The GDG judged the benefits of BPaL with linezolid 600–26 to be large and the undesirable effects moderate compared to the WHO-recommended 9-month regimen with ethionamide. The certainty of evidence was very low. Based on this, the panel concluded that the balance of health effects likely favors BPaL with linezolid 600–26. Therefore, the use of the 6-month treatment regimen composed of bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid (BPaL) rather than the 9-month regimen (with ethionamide) is suggested in patients with MDR/RR-TB without resistance to fluoroquinolones, who have either had no previous exposure to bedaquiline and linezolid or have been exposed for less than 1 month. The BPaLM regimen arm of the TB-PRACTECAL trial, which included patients with MDR/RR-TB with or without fluoroquinolone resistance (MDR/RR-TB or pre-XDR-TB), was compared with the comparator arm of the TB-PRACTECAL trial. This comparator arm comprised MDR/RR-TB or pre-XDR-TB patients treated with multiple local standard-of-care (SoC) regimens recommended by WHO at the time of the trial, including a 9–12-month injectable-containing regimen, an 18–24-month WHO-recommended regimen (pre-2019), a 9–12-month all-oral regimen, and an 18–20-month all-oral regimen. The primary analysis was conducted at 72 weeks post-treatment initiation. The GDG judged the benefits of BPaLM to be large and the undesirable effects trivial compared to WHO-recommended SoC regimens. The certainty of evidence was very low. Based on this, the panel concluded that the balance of health effects likely favors the BPaLM regimen. Therefore, the use of the 6-month treatment regimen composed of bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, and moxifloxacin (BPaLM) rather than a 9-month or longer (18-month) regimen is suggested in MDR/RR-TB patients with or without resistance to fluoroquinolones, who have either had no previous exposure to bedaquiline and linezolid or have been exposed for less than 1 month.
